name: Kos
title: Holidays in Kos
intro: A flat, sunny Greek island of long sandy beaches, cycle paths and ancient ruins, a short boat ride from Turkey. Here's what Kos is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: A white Orthodox chapel with a blue dome above the sea on the island of Kos
facts_note: Most flights run from May to October. The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June, September and early October are best, hot and sunny with a warm sea and fewer crowds. July and August are hottest, but the north wind keeps it bearable. From November to April most hotels close and there are few flights.

things.name: Kos Town
things.blurb: A harbour town with a Knights' castle, ancient ruins in the streets and lively squares.

things.name: Asklepion
things.blurb: The ancient healing sanctuary linked to Hippocrates, on terraces above the coast.

things.name: Paradise beach
things.blurb: Soft sand and clear water on the south coast, with bubbles rising from the seabed.

things.name: Cycling
things.blurb: Kos is flat, and bike lanes run along the coast from Kos Town.

things.name: Zia
things.blurb: A mountain village famous for its sunset views over the sea.

things.name: Bodrum or Nisyros
things.blurb: Ferries reach Bodrum in Turkey or the volcano island of Nisyros.

faqs.question: Which part of Kos is best to stay?
faqs.answer: Kos Town for a mix of sights and nightlife, Kefalos and Kardamena for beaches, and Marmari or Tigaki for quiet sand and calm sea.

faqs.question: Is Kos good for a beach holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. The island is ringed with sandy beaches, many shallow and calm.

faqs.question: Can you go to Turkey from Kos?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ferries to Bodrum take about 30 to 45 minutes. Take your passport.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Kos?
faqs.answer: A week gives you time for beaches, Kos Town, the Asklepion and a boat trip.
